exposure: sequential labor induction with prostaglandins and oxytocin
previous cesarean delivery with severe postpartum hemorrhage
outcome: complete uterine rupture (tearing of all uterine wall layers, including serosa and membranes)
cohort: The study included 1,317,967 women without previous cesarean delivery and 57,859 women with previous cesarean delivery who gave birth after starting labor in Norway between 1967 and 2008.
finding: Sequential labor induction with prostaglandins and oxytocin was the strongest risk factor for complete uterine rupture in both women with intact and scarred uteri.
mod_finding: For women with a previous cesarean delivery, an interdelivery interval of <16 months and a previous cesarean delivery with severe postpartum hemorrhage increased the risk of uterine rupture.
